The boson \(X\) has a mass of \(6\,\text{GeV}\). At lowest order, it decays into fermion–antifermion pairs \(f\bar{f}\) via the Yukawa-like interaction \(\mathcal{L} \supset -\lambda_f \bar{\psi}_f X \psi_f\). A decay \(X \to f\bar{f}\) is kinematically allowed if \(2m_f < m_X = 6\,\text{GeV}\), i.e., \(m_f < 3\,\text{GeV}\).

Approximate fermion masses:
- Quarks: \(u\) (\(\sim2.3\,\text{MeV}\)), \(d\) (\(\sim4.8\,\text{MeV}\)), \(s\) (\(\sim95\,\text{MeV}\)), \(c\) (\(\sim1.28\,\text{GeV}\)), \(b\) (\(\sim4.18\,\text{GeV}\)), \(t\) (\(\sim173\,\text{GeV}\)).
- Charged leptons: \(e\) (\(0.511\,\text{MeV}\)), \(\mu\) (\(105.7\,\text{MeV}\)), \(\tau\) (\(1.78\,\text{GeV}\)).

Fermions with \(m_f < 3\,\text{GeV}\) are \(u, d, s, c, e, \mu, \tau\). The \(b\) and \(t\) quarks are too heavy. Among the options, only (D) lists exactly these allowed fermions without including any kinematically forbidden ones.

Answer: D
